before: // Hold: ceiling and SS_done keep their values for all of S_RUN.
after: // Hold: ceiling and SS_done keep their values for all of S_RUN.
proposal.description: A max_on_limit raised during S_RUN widens the held ceiling at once, as if only a lowered limit had to wait for the next ramp, instead of every change being deferred to the next soft start.
proposal.reason: If the host raises MAX_ON while the supervisor is in S_RUN, max_on_counts jumps straight to the new limit under the running loop. It should keep the ceiling the ramp reached until the next soft start re-ramps to it.

proposal.description: On the at-target branch SS_done waits for a PWM falling edge, as if it were a ceiling update that must land between pulses, while the clamp itself still acts on the clock it is found.
proposal.reason: When max_on_limit equals the MIN_ON_CNT floor, or is lowered below the ceiling mid-ramp, the ceiling is clamped at once but SS_done rises only at the next switching-cycle boundary, not on the next clock. That delays the handover to S_RUN, and the header requires a floor-level limit to finish on the first clock of S_SS.

proposal.description: The step-window counter wraps at or past its terminal count (the at-or-past form of the target test), while the ceiling-step test still requires the count to equal it.
proposal.reason: If cycles_per_step is lowered below the running count in S_SS, the counter wraps to 0 at the next PWM falling edge without a ceiling step, so the ramp loses that window. The original instead keeps counting up to the counter's natural wrap. Either way the time at which max_on_counts next widens is different.
